checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are largely accurate. The classification of the 'Massive installation' checkpoint as untestable is technically correct due to framing, though the scale relative to background trees provides strong implicit evidence. All functional and geometric checkpoints for the visible portions of the telescope are correctly marked as present. The Router did not miss any obvious structural failures in its initial pass.
artifact_review: The Router reported no artifacts. However, the Perceptual Quality Auditor identified 'slight compression' (severity 0.2). While minor, this indicates the image is not pristine. More importantly, a visual re-inspection reveals subtle inconsistencies in the mesh texture on the dish surface; the grid pattern becomes slightly irregular and 'mushy' near the rim, which is a common AI artifact when rendering fine repetitive structures on curved surfaces. The Geometric Depth Auditor's clean depth map suggests good overall 3D structure, but it cannot detect these texture-level anomalies. The severity of the mesh irregularity is low (approx 1.5) but present.
alignment_reasoning: The Fine Grained Classifier confirmed the class with high confidence (Logit 7.78 vs 4.9 for next best). All visible diagnostic checkpoints (parabolic curve, feed horn, mount, mesh material) are present and structurally plausible. The image aligns extremely well with the taxonomy of a radio telescope.
artifact_reasoning: While the global structure is sound (supported by Depth and Topology experts), there are minor quality issues. The Perceptual Auditor flagged slight compression. Visually, the mesh texture on the dish shows minor warping/inconsistency near the edges, preventing a perfect artifact score. It is far superior to the 'mid' reference but lacks the absolute crispness of the 'high' reference.
